name: Domestic-individual convenience quota purchase + bank wire
category: A. Individual current-account and provider routes
fit: Account classified as 境内个人 (PRC ID); genuine current-account purpose; unused annual quota.
limit: USD 50,000 equivalent per person per calendar year for purchase inside the convenience quota; above quota needs authenticity documents or another route. Outbound remittance from an existing FX account has a separate USD 50,000/day ID-only threshold.
cost: BOC and HSBC local wire charges are tariff-derived in the cost ladder; FX spread is a BOC board proxy only; personal tax blank.
pros: Simple inside quota; bank executes purchase and wire together; capped wire commission.
cons: Annual quota is not a universal outbound ceiling; false purpose declarations are prohibited; branch may refuse; larger balances need documents/approval.

steps.action: Confirm the bank’s identity classification and remaining annual convenience quota.
steps.evidence: Art.54 quota applies to domestic-individual purchase; Art.37 defines domestic individual by PRC ID.

steps.action: Complete the individual FX purchase application with the genuine current-account purpose and buy USD inside the unused quota.
steps.evidence: Arts.55–57 require ID and purchase application inside quota.

steps.action: Submit the outbound remittance instruction with payee name, account/IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, bank address and purpose; provide authenticity documents if above the applicable threshold.
steps.evidence: Art.64 distinguishes USD 50,000/day ID-only outbound from above-threshold documentary review.

steps.action: Choose SHA/BEN/OUR or full-amount-arrival option, confirm all charges in writing, send and retain the purchase memo and wire receipt.
steps.evidence: BOC/HSBC tariffs list cable, commission and optional full-delivery charges; correspondent/receiving fees may remain.

name: Overseas-individual documented current-account income purchase + remittance (Art.59)
category: A. Individual current-account and provider routes
fit: Account classified as 境外个人 (passport/HK-Macao-Taiwan permit); lawful current-account RMB income earned in China (e.g. salary) with source and tax evidence.
limit: No annual cap is stated in Art.59 for documented lawful current-account RMB income; permanent-residence-card holders use the convenience quota. Bank accepts only proven amount.
cost: Same bank tariffs as M01; no transfer tax identified on the exchange itself; underlying IIT and US tax depend on facts.
pros: Strongest text-based route for documented China salary; can exceed USD 50,000; repeat salary facilitation at same bank.
cons: Document-heavy; branch practice varies; capital proceeds/savings without income proof do not qualify; classification conflict with one-year residence rule.

steps.action: Ask the bank in writing to process the purchase under Art.59 as an overseas individual and confirm which identity document governs the account.
steps.evidence: Art.37 passport definition; Art.59 source-material route; F01 conflict must be resolved by the branch/SAFE.

steps.action: Assemble passport, employment/contract evidence, payroll records, PRC tax vouchers or electronic tax records, and source-of-funds explanation matching the RMB amount.
steps.evidence: Art.59 requires ID and source materials including tax vouchers; CN06 removes tax voucher only where income is not taxable.

steps.action: For repeat salary purchases within contract validity at the same bank, invoke the 2021 facilitation to avoid duplicate documents; otherwise submit the full file.
steps.evidence: 汇发〔2021〕13号 repeat salary/tuition facilitation.

steps.action: Buy USD against the approved amount, remit to your own overseas account or genuine payee, and retain the bank’s approved source file and receipts.
steps.evidence: Art.59 purchase/remittance; provider guidance restates documentary review.

name: Remit existing USD from a domestic FX account
category: A. Individual current-account and provider routes
fit: Funds are already foreign currency in a domestic individual FX savings account; genuine current-account outbound purpose.
limit: Domestic individual: USD 50,000 equivalent/day cumulative on ID, above with documents. Overseas individual: FX-account outbound on ID. Cash withdrawal tier is USD 10,000/day.
cost: Bank wire tariff applies; no CNY→USD spread at the remittance step because conversion already happened; original conversion cost/tax still matters.
pros: Avoids a second conversion; per-day threshold is not the annual purchase quota; overseas-individual account simpler.
cons: Does not solve CNY conversion; purpose/authenticity still reviewed; cash and transfer thresholds differ.

steps.action: Confirm the account holds 现汇 (spot FX), not 现钞 (cash) or RMB, and identify the original conversion/source records.
steps.evidence: Art.64/65 apply to FX-account outbound; cash rules are separate.

steps.action: For a domestic individual, keep ID-only outbound within USD 50,000 equivalent per day or prepare transaction-amount documents above it; for an overseas individual, present ID.
steps.evidence: Art.64 domestic tiers; Art.65 overseas individual ID-only.

steps.action: Submit payee/SWIFT details and genuine purpose, choose charge option, and remit; retain receipt and source records.
steps.evidence: Provider tariffs govern local charges; SAFE requires authenticity.

name: Wise CNY salary route to own USD account
category: A. Individual current-account and provider routes
fit: Non-mainland Chinese personal customer who works/worked in China; valid PRC tax record within last 3 years; recipient account in own name.
limit: Bank-app funding max CNY 300,000 per transfer; Alipay max CNY 50,000; overall limit generally after-tax China salary proven by tax records; SkyRemit transfers share the remaining limit.
cost: One live 200,000 CNY bank-funded quote captured; no 40-point fee curve inferred; ladder Wise total blank.
pros: Digital onboarding; own-name delivery; transparent fee quote; large-amount discount.
cons: Not a general savings/property route; tax-record limit; shared SkyRemit limit; dynamic pricing; bank-app funding quirks.

steps.action: Register a personal Wise account and complete first-time verification (provider says 1–2 working days).
steps.evidence: Wise CNY guide verification and eligibility.

steps.action: Upload passport/identity and PRC tax records showing taxes paid within the accepted window; wait for the assigned overall sending limit.
steps.evidence: Wise limit is based on annual income, tax paid and years proven; SkyRemit usage reduces it.

steps.action: Create a CNY→USD transfer to an account you own, choose bank-app or Alipay funding, and review the exact fee/rate/limit before confirming.
steps.evidence: Wise own-name rule and per-transfer funding caps; live quote is transaction-specific.

steps.action: Fund from the Chinese bank app/Alipay exactly as instructed, track conversion, and reconcile the USD receipt and fee statement.
steps.evidence: Wise guide describes bank-app funding, safeguarding and conversion timing.

name: SkyRemit CNY salary route to own overseas account
category: A. Individual current-account and provider routes
fit: Expats/HK-Macao-Taiwan residents in China with identity and tax invoice/work certificate; provider and bank accept the source file.
limit: CNY 500–300,000 per transfer; Wise guide says SkyRemit usage shares the Wise overall after-tax salary limit.
cost: CNY 79 fixed fee plus observed 0.27% FX markup scenario; ladder is illustrative, not an executable quote.
pros: Mobile/PC, 7×24, fast delivery, multiple funding methods; fixed fee transparent.
cons: Per-transfer cap forces multiple transfers; shared Wise limit; marketing superiority claim not used; widget inconsistency flagged; not a quota bypass.

steps.action: Register with Chinese mobile/email and complete identity verification (passport, work visa/permit).
steps.evidence: SkyRemit four-step onboarding.

steps.action: Upload tax invoice/work certificate and source evidence; obtain the provider’s approved sending limit and confirm it does not exceed the lawful documented income.
steps.evidence: SkyRemit verification; Wise guide confirms shared limit; SAFE Art.59 substance still governs.

steps.action: Initiate a transfer within CNY 300,000, select Alipay/WeChat/bank funding, review final rate and CNY 79 fee, and confirm payee details.
steps.evidence: SkyRemit product terms and calculator.

steps.action: Fund the transfer, track receipt (normally 24–48h per provider), and retain rate/fee confirmation for tax basis and reporting.
steps.evidence: SkyRemit delivery claim; records needed for US/PRC reporting.

name: HSBC Global Transfer / same-name overseas HSBC account
category: A. Individual current-account and provider routes
fit: Eligible HSBC China customer with linked same-name overseas HSBC account; product and regulatory purpose accepted.
limit: Product-specific limits and eligibility; not a blanket exemption from SAFE purchase/remittance rules.
cost: HSBC tariff waives certain HSBC local fees for qualifying same-name Global Transfers; ordinary Premier/Advance third-party wires are not universally free; FX spread and account fees unverified.
pros: Can reduce HSBC local wire/cable charges; integrated same-name transfer.
cons: Premier eligibility/monthly fee or balance requirement; overseas account opening rules; correspondent/receiving charges may remain; not a legal quota bypass.

steps.action: Confirm HSBC China customer tier and whether the intended transfer is a qualifying same-name Global Transfer, not an ordinary third-party wire.
steps.evidence: Tariff distinguishes private banking, Premier/Advance, Elite and product-specific waivers.

steps.action: Open/link the overseas HSBC account through HSBC’s accepted witnessing/onboarding process and satisfy local account rules.
steps.evidence: HSBC tariff overseas-account appointment and witnessing items; SAFE Art.79 visa condition for witnessing.

steps.action: Purchase/remit only against a lawful documented purpose and quota/Art.59 route; select the linked own-name account in online banking.
steps.evidence: SAFE rules govern purchase/remittance; provider product does not override them.

steps.action: Before confirming, obtain written confirmation of HSBC local fee waiver, FX rate, and any non-HSBC correspondent/receiving charges.
steps.evidence: Tariff says free excludes non-HSBC charges; full-delivery pre-charge may apply.

name: BOC overseas-account witnessing (account-opening aid, not a transfer route)
category: A. Individual current-account and provider routes
fit: Customer needs an overseas BOC account and holds a foreign visa valid at least three months.
limit: SAFE Art.79 visa condition; overseas account approval is separate.
cost: BOC tariff lists witnessing ≤CNY 400; account fees and transfer costs unverified.
pros: May help establish a lawful destination account; fee cap published.
cons: Not itself a CNY→USD remittance; overseas KYC/eligibility; visa condition; account fees unknown.

steps.action: Confirm the foreign visa is valid for at least three months and ask BOC whether the destination account/product is available for witnessing.
steps.evidence: SAFE Art.79 minimum visa validity.

steps.action: Book the witnessing service, present identity/visa documents, and obtain the tariff-quoted fee (≤CNY 400).
steps.evidence: BOC personal tariff witnessing item.

steps.action: Complete overseas account approval separately; then use a lawful purchase/remittance route (M01–M03) to fund it.
steps.evidence: Account opening does not create FX permission; SAFE purchase/remittance rules still apply.

name: Emigration property transfer (移民财产转移)
category: B. Capital, property and corporate routes
fit: Natural person who emigrated from mainland China / settled in HK-Macao-Taiwan and owned lawful China property before acquiring immigrant status; hukou cancellation and foreign residence proof.
limit: One-time application for the whole amount; staging: first ≤50%, after 1 year ≤half remainder, after 2 years balance; ≤CNY 200,000 may go at once after approval. Provincial approval ≤CNY 500,000; above SAFE HQ.
cost: SAFE administrative fee none in service guide; bank FX/wire charges and underlying taxes still apply; personal total blank.
pros: Express route for pre-emigration property; can move large documented balances; no SAFE service fee in guide.
cons: Not available merely because one holds a US passport; staging delays; hukou/consular/tax documents; funds to own overseas account only.

steps.action: Confirm eligibility: property owned before immigrant status, hukou cancellation, and foreign citizenship/permanent residence or HK-Macao-Taiwan settlement.
steps.evidence: 2004 Measures and 2026 SAFE definition FAQ.

steps.action: Apply once to the SAFE office of former hukou locality with application form, identity, consular residence proof/apostille, property/income evidence and tax certificate.
steps.evidence: Service guide document list; jurisdiction FAQ.

steps.action: Obtain the capital-account approval and observe staging/approval-tier limits; do not split applications to evade staging.
steps.evidence: 2004 Measures one-time application and staging.

steps.action: Through the approved bank, purchase FX and remit to your own overseas account in permitted stages; retain approval and tax records.
steps.evidence: 2004 Measures own-account destination; service guide in-person handling.

name: Inheritance property transfer (继承财产转移)
category: B. Capital, property and corporate routes
fit: Foreign citizen or HK-Macao-Taiwan resident who lawfully inherited mainland China property and realised it.
limit: Apply to decedent’s former hukou locality; same property-transfer staging/approval framework; amount limited to lawful inherited realised property.
cost: SAFE administrative fee none in service guide; bank charges and underlying inheritance/property taxes unverified; personal total blank.
pros: Express route for foreign heirs; can combine multiple decedents at one locality.
cons: Requires inheritance公证/will and decedent property proof; tax certificate; not a general savings route; staging may apply.

steps.action: Establish heir status (foreign passport/HK-Macao-Taiwan documents) and lawful inheritance through notarised inheritance/will documents.
steps.evidence: Inheritance service guide identity and inheritance proof.

steps.action: Collect decedent property-rights evidence and the competent tax authority’s tax certificate (or electronic verification).
steps.evidence: Service guide materials list.

steps.action: Apply to SAFE at the decedent’s former hukou locality; if multiple decedents, choose one locality for a combined application.
steps.evidence: Jurisdiction FAQ.

steps.action: After approval, use the bank to purchase/remit to the applicant’s own overseas account within the approved amount and staging.
steps.evidence: 2004 Measures and service guide.

name: Overseas individual’s China property-sale proceeds
category: B. Capital, property and corporate routes
fit: Overseas individual sells domestic commercial property; title transfer completed; tax certificate matches remittance amount.
limit: Remittance cannot exceed sale price less taxes/fees of the transfer; co-owners limited to their share; tax-certificate amount must match; title transfer must be completed before outbound.
cost: Underlying property-transfer IIT may apply to gain; bank FX/wire charges apply; personal total blank.
pros: Express current property-sale route; 2025 operational guide clarifies cap and documents.
cons: Not the 2004 emigration route; requires completed sale/title transfer and tax match; gain/tax facts unknown; other sale taxes unverified.

steps.action: Complete the property sale and title transfer; obtain contract/registration, tax certificate, property invoice and title proof.
steps.evidence: 2025 operational guide requires completed title transfer and matching tax certificate; HSBC guide lists documents.

steps.action: Calculate the maximum outbound amount as sale price minus taxes/fees included in this transfer (and your co-owner share if any).
steps.evidence: Operational guide cap and tax-certificate match.

steps.action: Apply through the bank for purchase/remittance under the overseas-individual property-sale rules; provide公证授权委托书 if delegating.
steps.evidence: Operational guide delegation and bank review; Measures Art.22.

steps.action: Remit the approved net proceeds to your overseas account and retain sale/tax/bank records for PRC and US reporting.
steps.evidence: Operational guide bank reporting; US reporting may apply to accounts/gains.

name: FIE dividend / profit repatriation to foreign investor
category: B. Capital, property and corporate routes
fit: Foreign investor receives lawfully distributable profits from a foreign-invested enterprise; corporate, not personal savings.
limit: Current capital-account guide locates profit remittance at §7.12; full current checklist not retrieved from PDF; historical guide lists resolution, audited accounts and tax filing.
cost: Corporate dividend withholding/IIT and treaty facts unverified; bank charges blank; no personal ladder amount.
pros: Express corporate profit route where profits exist; treaty may cap source tax for qualifying residents.
cons: Requires corporate profits, loss make-up, audit/resolution and tax filing; not a way to move personal savings; current checklist gap.

steps.action: Confirm the enterprise has distributable after-tax profits after making up prior losses and obtain the board/shareholder profit-distribution resolution.
steps.evidence: Historical/current guide framework; IIT law taxes dividend income; full 2024 checklist flagged.

steps.action: Prepare audited financial statements and the competent tax authority’s outward-payment tax filing/withholding evidence.
steps.evidence: Profit-remittance documentary framework; treaty relief requires facts.

steps.action: Submit the bank’s authenticity/tax review and remit to the foreign investor’s account; retain corporate and tax records.
steps.evidence: Capital-account guide profit-remittance section; FX Regulation current/capital authenticity.

name: FIE liquidation / capital reduction repatriation
category: B. Capital, property and corporate routes
fit: Foreign-invested enterprise lawfully terminated/liquidated or capital reduced; foreign investor’s RMB proceeds after tax.
limit: State Council Regulation Art.22 paragraph 3 permits conversion/remittance after liquidation and tax payment; capital-guide divestment section locates bank control-table process.
cost: Corporate/liquidation taxes and bank charges unverified; personal total blank.
pros: Express statutory entitlement for terminated FIE proceeds; can move investor’s share.
cons: Corporate liquidation is costly/slow; tax and creditor process; not personal savings; exact bank checklist partially unverified.

steps.action: Complete lawful liquidation/capital reduction, creditor and tax procedures, and determine the foreign investor’s net RMB entitlement.
steps.evidence: Regulation Art.22 paragraph 3 requires liquidation and tax payment.

steps.action: Obtain the capital-account business registration/control information required by the bank for divestment/liquidation outflow.
steps.evidence: Capital Guide §7.10 locator; exact current checklist flagged where not retrieved.

steps.action: Bank reviews authenticity, converts the investor’s RMB and remits to the foreign investor’s overseas account; complete balance-of-payments reporting.
steps.evidence: Regulation entitlement and capital-guide framework.

name: Genuine current-account service/trade or income payment abroad
category: B. Capital, property and corporate routes
fit: A real cross-border service, trade, royalty, tuition, medical or other current-account obligation exists; not a disguised capital transfer.
limit: No universal USD 50,000 ceiling for genuine current-account payments; documentary authenticity and tax filing where applicable (service-trade filing threshold/exemptions need confirmation).
cost: Underlying VAT/IIT/withholding and bank charges depend on transaction; blank.
pros: Lawful current-account payments are not restricted in principle; can fit genuine obligations.
cons: Cannot invent a service to move savings; tax filing/withholding may apply; contract/invoice evidence required.

steps.action: Identify the genuine current-account obligation and collect contract, invoice, tax and counterparty evidence matching the payment amount.
steps.evidence: FX Regulation Art.5/current-account authenticity; current guide documentary review.

steps.action: Determine whether outward-payment tax filing/withholding applies and complete it before bank processing where required.
steps.evidence: Service-trade tax filing is transaction-specific; threshold/exemptions flagged F19.

steps.action: Purchase FX if needed under the applicable individual/corporate route and remit to the genuine counterparty with purpose documents.
steps.evidence: Current-account purchase/remittance rules; no disguised capital transfer.

name: Cross-border e-commerce / market procurement / border trade settlement
category: B. Capital, property and corporate routes
fit: Genuine qualifying trade activity with electronic transaction data or evidence; not personal savings.
limit: Art.66 allows settlement outside the convenience quota for qualifying e-commerce/market-procurement/border trade based on actual transaction volume.
cost: Trade taxes, platform/payment fees and bank charges unverified; blank.
pros: Does not consume USD 50,000 convenience quota; suited to real traders.
cons: Requires genuine trade data; AML/authenticity review; not a personal remittance workaround.

steps.action: Confirm the activity qualifies under Art.66 and gather platform/transaction/customs evidence showing actual trade volume.
steps.evidence: Art.66 evidence-based settlement outside quota.

steps.action: Use the qualified bank/payment institution’s trade-settlement process, declare the true trade purpose and complete applicable tax filings.
steps.evidence: Current-account authenticity and tax rules.

steps.action: Settle/remit only against verified transactions and retain electronic data for bank and tax review.
steps.evidence: Art.66 and FX Regulation authenticity.

name: Reconversion / refund of unused RMB from a prior FX exchange
category: C. Cash, cards, domestic and closed-loop paths
fit: Unused RMB remains from a prior lawful FX exchange and original exchange memo is available.
limit: Art.60: original exchange memo valid 24 months; small daily reconversion tiers (USD 500/day; USD 1,000 at exit ports) without memo in specified cases.
cost: Bank spread/fees may apply; original conversion cost already incurred; personal tax blank.
pros: Restores unused FX without a new income source; express rule.
cons: Time-limited; memo required for larger reconversion; not a route for ordinary RMB savings.

steps.action: Locate the original FX exchange memo and confirm the unused RMB amount and 24-month validity.
steps.evidence: Art.60 reconversion rule.

steps.action: Present ID and memo at the bank; if within the small daily tier without memo, confirm the applicable USD 500/1,000 exit-port condition.
steps.evidence: Art.60 daily tiers.

steps.action: Reconvert only the eligible unused amount and retain the new receipt; remit/deposit/carry subject to the usual rules.
steps.evidence: Art.60 and CN06 use of purchased FX.

name: Carry foreign-currency cash out of China and declare into the US
category: C. Cash, cards, domestic and closed-loop paths
fit: Physical USD cash lawfully obtained; travel and permits feasible; US declaration if >USD 10,000.
limit: China: ≤USD 5,000 no permit; USD 5,000–10,000 bank permit; >USD 10,000 SAFE permit in principle; repeat-exit lower tiers. US: >USD 10,000 family aggregate requires FinCEN 105.
cost: BOC permit fee CNY 10 waived through 2026-12-31; travel/insurance/cash spread unverified; personal tax blank.
pros: No wire corridor; immediate physical possession; permit fee may be waived.
cons: Impractical/risky for large balances; permits and declarations; forfeiture risk; cash spread may differ; not a way to evade reporting.

steps.action: Determine the cash amount and obtain the correct Chinese carrying permit: none ≤USD 5,000, bank permit USD 5,000–10,000, SAFE permit above USD 10,000 in principle; check repeat-exit tiers.
steps.evidence: ICBC guidance implementing carry rules; BOC tariff permit fee/waiver.

steps.action: Carry the permit, ID and source records; declare truthfully to Chinese customs where required and do not structure trips to evade limits.
steps.evidence: Carry rules and anti-evasion framework; structuring flagged as prohibited.

steps.action: On US arrival, if currency/monetary instruments exceed USD 10,000 in aggregate (including family), file FinCEN 105 with CBP.
steps.evidence: CBP reporting rule; reporting is not a tax.

steps.action: Deposit or hold the cash lawfully and retain source/declaration records for tax basis and FBAR/8938 analysis.
steps.evidence: US reporting and §988 basis records.

name: Overseas ATM withdrawal using a China-issued card
category: C. Cash, cards, domestic and closed-loop paths
fit: China-issued card with overseas ATM cash access; within annual/daily caps.
limit: All domestic cards combined: CNY 100,000/person/year; each card CNY 10,000/day; over-limit suspension this year and next.
cost: BOC UnionPay CNY 12+1% cap CNY 112; from 2026-11-11 Mastercard/VISA 2.5% min USD 3 max USD 40; foreign ATM surcharge and card FX fee unverified.
pros: Useful for small travel cash; issuer tariff published for BOC.
cons: Annual cap is far below USD 400,000; suspension risk; foreign ATM surcharge; not a bulk repatriation route.

steps.action: Check the card network, remaining annual CNY 100,000 person-wide cash quota and CNY 10,000/card/day limit.
steps.evidence: SAFE 2017 notice.

steps.action: Confirm issuer fee (UnionPay vs Mastercard/VISA and effective date) and the foreign ATM’s own surcharge before withdrawal.
steps.evidence: BOC current tariff and 2026-11-11 announcement; foreign surcharge extra.

steps.action: Withdraw within limits, retain receipts, and report/declare cash if later transported across borders above thresholds.
steps.evidence: SAFE caps; CBP reporting if transported into US >USD 10,000.

name: Spend abroad directly on a China-issued card (not cash repatriation)
category: C. Cash, cards, domestic and closed-loop paths
fit: Genuine personal overseas spending; card accepted; not a cash-out or investment purchase.
limit: Card spending abroad does not consume the USD 50,000 purchase quota and is distinct from the CNY 100,000 overseas cash-withdrawal cap.
cost: Card network/issuer FX fee and merchant pricing unverified; no wire fee; not a USD balance transfer.
pros: Avoids a separate wire for consumption; quota distinction is explicit.
cons: Does not create a US USD deposit; merchant/network spread; cash-advance fees differ; investment/insurance purchases may be restricted.

steps.action: Confirm the transaction is genuine consumption, not cash withdrawal or a prohibited capital/investment purchase.
steps.evidence: SAFE distinguishes card spending from cash withdrawal; purchase-purpose restrictions apply.

steps.action: Check issuer/network foreign-transaction fee and whether merchant offers dynamic currency conversion; choose the cheaper lawful option.
steps.evidence: Issuer tariffs publish ATM fees but card purchase FX fees were not verified; flagged.

steps.action: Pay the merchant directly and retain statements; do not use refunds or fake merchants to extract cash.
steps.evidence: Anti-evasion/authenticity framework.

name: Western Union China outbound (partner bank / cash pickup)
category: C. Cash, cards, domestic and closed-loop paths

cost: Domestic bank fees unverified; no outbound conversion cost at this step.

steps.action: Submit the bank’s domestic FX transfer instruction with relationship/source evidence and retain receipt.

name: Wealth Management Connect Southbound (closed-loop investment)

steps.evidence: HKMA closed-loop requirement.
